old:
Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles in a dilute solution, not on their nature. There are four.

Relative lowering of vapour pressure: equals the mole fraction of the solute.

Elevation of boiling point: the solution boils at a higher temperature because its vapour pressure is lower. Here $\Delta T_b = K_b m$.

Depression of freezing point: the solution freezes at a lower temperature. Here $\Delta T_f = K_f m$.

$K_b$ and $K_f$ (in K kg $mol^{-1}$) depend only on the solvent. For water, $K_b = 0.52$ and $K_f = 1.86$.

Osmotic pressure ($\pi$): the extra pressure that must be applied to the solution side to stop solvent from flowing through a semipermeable membrane. Here $\pi = CRT$.

Solutions with equal osmotic pressure are isotonic. For example, 0.9% NaCl (normal saline) is isotonic with blood. Placed in a hypertonic solution, cells shrink (plasmolysis). Placed in a hypotonic solution, cells swell. Applying pressure greater than $\pi$ reverses the flow; this reverse osmosis is used for desalination.
new:
Colligative properties depend only on the number of solute particles in a dilute solution, not on their nature. There are four.

Relative lowering of vapour pressure: equals the mole fraction of the solute.

Elevation of boiling point: the solution boils at a higher temperature because its vapour pressure is lower. Here $\Delta T_b = K_b m$.

Depression of freezing point: the solution freezes at a lower temperature. Here $\Delta T_f = K_f m$.

$K_b$ and $K_f$ (in K kg $mol^{-1}$) depend only on the solvent. For water, $K_b = 0.52$ and $K_f = 1.86$.

Osmotic pressure ($\pi$): the extra pressure that must be applied to the solution side to stop solvent from flowing through a semipermeable membrane. Here $\pi = CRT$.

Solutions with equal osmotic pressure are isotonic. For example, 0.9% NaCl (normal saline) is isotonic with blood. Placed in a hypertonic solution (more than 0.9% NaCl), cells lose water and shrink. For plant cells this is called plasmolysis; for red blood cells it is crenation. In a hypotonic solution, cells swell and may burst. Applying pressure greater than $\pi$ reverses the flow; this reverse osmosis is used for desalination.
fixes: Plasmolysis applies to plant cells; shrinking red blood cells is crenation

old: Of the same solutions, the one with the most particles has the lowest freezing point and the highest boiling point
new: For solutions in the same solvent with equal molality, the one giving the most solute particles (largest $i \times m$) has the lowest freezing point and the highest boiling point
fixes: Clarify that the comparison holds only for the same solvent and equal molality
